title: Approval path and LLM costing clarity session
summary: Procurement-led call to map Arcadia's internal approval lanes for MSA/DPA and to reconcile LLM unit economics with finance. Redwood AE/SE covered hosting vs dedicated deployment, egress and KMS options, SLA tiers, and pilot pricing. Action items agreed: Redwood to send pricing scenarios, SOC2/DPA pack, and an example canary rollout plan. Arcadia to surface stakeholder sign-off timeline and provide a list of sensitive datasets for compliance review.
action_items: Maya Thompson - Send three pricing scenarios (hosted, dedicated small reserve, reserved + burst) - due 2025-12-03
Liam Chen - Provide SOC2 summary, security architecture diagram, and DPA template redline guide - due 2025-12-04
Sofia Alvarez - Share internal approver list and expected approval dates - due 2025-12-05
Raj Patel - Clarify KMS/policy requirements and list of regulated datasets - due 2025-12-07
next_steps: Redwood to post pricing spreadsheet and short pilot SOW
Customer to review SOC2 and DPA materials and flag exceptions
Schedule technical ridealong / benchmark with SE (45-60m) next week
Finance to confirm cost model assumptions and preferred billing cadence
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Arcadia Procurement), Raj (Arcadia Security), Ellen (Arcadia PM), Tom (Arcadia Finance)

Auto-summary (may be imperfect):
- Quick intro and approvals map
- Pricing math and pilot scope
- Security/egress/KMS clarifications

Transcript:
00:00 - Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through the approval path you mentioned in the intake and then map pricing scenarios to the lanes. is that still the ask?
00:18 - Sofia (Arcadia Procurement): yes exactly, the sourcing committee needs the MSA/DPA redline + cost for budgetary approval. timeline is kinda tight, we have a 2 week window to get to commercial committee.
00:32 - Maya: understood. quick intros? i'll be the AE and liaise on commercial, liam will handle the technical bits.
00:40 - Liam (Redwood SE): hi all, quick hello. i'll answer any infra, VPC, kms stuff.
00:47 - Ellen (Arcadia PM): thanks, i'm primarily looking for confirmation around data residency and any impact on latency if we go dedicated.
00:56 - Tom (Finance): and i'll be checking the per-token math and how egress might show up on our side.
01:05 - Maya: perfect. to frame the options: hosted (pay-as-you-go), dedicated (reserved capacity monthly), and private (VPC/on-prem) for highly regulated. pricing moves a lot by throughput and quantization but we'll give three scenarios.
01:22 - Raj (Arcadia Security): quick flag — we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed KMS, key rotation policies, and whether logs include full request bodies or only metadata.
01:34 - Liam: we support customer-managed KMS via KMS integrations for cloud providers and on-prem HSM in some private packages. logs can be configured; by default audit logs record request IDs and errors, full request capture is an opt-in with additional retention controls.
01:54 - Raj: opt-in capture, ok. we also need clarity on egress fees when data crosses regions — that is a procurement blocker.
02:05 - Maya: egress is charged when traffic leaves Redwood region to customer region or different cloud egress. for hosted, we can estimate typical egress bands; for dedicated you can negotiate fixed egress buckets in the reserved contract. we'll include that in the pricing doc.
02:20 - Sofia: and the MSA/DPA — do you accept limited redlines? our legal usually asks for specific DPA clauses around subprocessing and deletion timelines.
02:33 - Maya: yes, we accept limited redlines. our standard DPA covers sub-processors, deletion, and export controls. i'll have liam attach the DPA pack and a redline guide — note some enterprise clauses (like escrow) require additional approvals.
02:47 - Ellen: can you confirm SLA tiers and what counts toward downtime credits?
02:54 - Liam: SLA tiers are 99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99 depending on plan and dedicated guarantees. credits are pro-rated token-hour based and exclude customer network issues and scheduled maintenance. we can provide the exact escalation ladder in the SLA doc.
03:10 - Tom: what's the latency differential between hosted and dedicated for a 2k token seq?
03:18 - Liam: hosted median is typically 150-300ms per request for short seq but with 2k sequence and heavy KV usage you might see 400-800ms; dedicated on pinned GPUs reduces variance — think 30-40% lower p95 in our benchmarks. depends on batching and caching.
03:36 - Sofia: from procurement perspective we need the list of approvers. our process is: procurement -> security -> legal -> finance -> commercial committee. we need deliverables for each.
03:48 - Maya: got it. we'll map docs to each approver. for procurement you'll get pricing + egress examples; security gets SOC2, DPA redline notes, architecture diagram; legal gets MSA + negotiated redlines; finance gets cost modelling.
04:05 - Raj: on SOC2 — do you have a recent report and can we get a point-in-time summary?
04:11 - Liam: yes we have SOC2 Type II; i'll pull the summary and a list of controls. note that some accessibility in private deployments differs but we'll call that out.
04:23 - Ellen: can you share an example pilot SOW? we want to estimate run-time cost for a two-week pilot across 3 features.
04:30 - Maya: yes, we have a short pilot SOW template that outlines objectives, success criteria, data handling, and an estimate. we'll produce a pilot estimate based on conservative throughput.
04:42 - Tom: how are invoices typically structured for reserved capacity — monthly upfront or amortized?
04:46 - Maya: reserved is typically monthly invoiced; annual commits can be amortized quarterly as a commercial accommodation. we can show both cashflow views in the pricing spreadsheet.
04:58 - Raj: any limitations on bringing models or fine-tuning? some of our teams want to fine tune a small safety model.
05:06 - Liam: fine-tuning pathways exist but differ by deployment: hosted supports model variants and managed fine-tuning with controls; dedicated allows more flexibility but requires security review for training data residency. we'll flag the process.
05:22 - (crosstalk) Sofia: okay — budget sign-off is dec 12 is what we're aiming for, ideally.
05:28 - Maya: that's doable. we'll prioritize pricing + legal pack for you by end of week.
05:35 - Sofia: one more: data residency — do you have EU-only routing and assurances for deletion?
05:42 - Liam: we support region pinning for hosted and dedicated in EU regions; deletion policies can be contractualized in DPA with retention windows. physical egress logs are available on request.
05:57 - Ellen: can we get an anonymized benchmark of latency/throughput from a customer similar to us?
06:02 - Maya: yes, we can share a redacted benchmark readout from a retail customer — latency, cost per 1k tokens, and p95. i'll include that.
06:10 - Tom: pricing math: how do you break down per-token costs? compute vs model weights vs infra overhead?
06:17 - Liam: per-token rate includes GPU compute, memory pressure, and system orchestration overhead. for embeddings it's different. the spreadsheet will show unit breakdown and assumptions including sequence length distribution, batch factor, prefix caching effects.
06:32 - Sofia: any procurement-level references required? e.g., indemnity caps or insurance requirements?
06:38 - Maya: standard indemnity and insurance clauses are in the MSA; for higher caps we escalate to legal. we'll include current certs and insurance limits in the pack.
06:46 - (30:00 marker approximate, mid-call summary)
30:05 - Maya: quick recap — Redwood will: 1) Send pricing scenarios and cashflow views; 2) Share SOC2 summary, DPA and a redline guide; 3) Share pilot SOW and benchmark readout. Arcadia will: 1) Share approver list and timeline; 2) List of regulated datasets and kms needs; 3) Confirm budget target. any objections?
30:28 - Sofia: no objections, that aligns.
30:33 - Raj: just to reiterate, KMS integration detail and key custody are blockers for security sign-off.
30:40 - Liam: understoood — i'll include a KMS matrix showing supported providers, rotation, and what keys we hold vs what customer holds.
30:51 - Ellen: about SLA credits — do you have an example calculation we can show legal?
30:56 - Liam: yes we'll include the credit calc and an escalation ladder; also a canary/rollback plan for model rollouts so you can see mitigations.
31:08 - Tom: for finance, please show both committed monthly price and pay-as-you-go forecast for three usage bands.
31:16 - Maya: yes we'll include low/medium/high usage bands with assumptions.
31:22 - Sofia: any redlines to expect on the MSA from your side?
31:26 - Maya: typical enterprise asks we see: data residency commitments, audit rights, subprocessor lists; we can accept many but some clauses (infinite indemnity, unilateral audit access) will require exec sign-off. we'll call those out.
31:40 - Raj: is there MFA/SSO support for console? our vendor policy requires SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning.
31:47 - Liam: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. we'll include a short implementation ETA in the technical appendix.
31:57 - Ellen: can we get a dry-run security questionnaire (SIG) filled?
32:02 - Maya: we can start with a short vendor security pack and then the full SIG if needed; liam will attach the vendor pack.
32:10 - (small interruption, background noise)
32:21 - Sofia: about escalation — who is our redwood contact post-sign? we'd need an SEA or CSM.
32:28 - Maya: i'll be your commercial owner through contracting; post-sign you'll get a named CSM and an onboarding SE.
32:34 - Tom: for the pilot SOW — any cost cap we can set so finance isn't surprised?
32:40 - Maya: yes we can define a pilot not-to-exceed and include an approval threshold for overages.
32:46 - Raj: one more technical: do you support dedicated VPC peering or private interconnect for data plane?
32:53 - Liam: yes, dedicated supports VPC peering and private interconnect options, depending on region. private on-prem is an option but with longer lead time.
33:05 - Ellen: timeline question — if we sign pilot by mid-december, what's a typical time-to-prod if all goes well?
33:12 - Liam: pilot 2-4 weeks, then another 4-8 weeks for production depending on integrations and security review. so earliest mid-late feb for a simple path.
33:25 - Sofia: procurement needs to see a clear timeline mapping MSA closure to pilot start — can you include dependencies in the SOW?
33:33 - Maya: yes we'll show dependencies and a gating checklist.
33:38 - (rough technical aside on quantization and token costing)
40:10 - Liam: to reduce per-token spend we typically suggest 8-bit quantization and KV prefix caching; that can reduce cost by 30% in some workloads but has small impact on quality in edge cases.
40:29 - Tom: can you quantify the cache hit expectations?
40:34 - Liam: depends on session reuse; with conversational UX you'd typically get 40-60% effective prefix reuse if the UX is sessioned, which reduces compute. we'll include an example with math in the pricing doc.
40:50 - Sofia: anything else from procurement? no.
40:55 - Maya: final quick ask — can Arcadia share the list of sensitive datasets so we can do a quick compliance call?
41:03 - Raj: yes i'll send a redacted list.
41:08 - Maya: great. we'll wrap up with next steps; thanks everyone.
41:14 - (end of recorded exchange, remaining minutes used for 1:1 clarifications and follow-ups)

Closing recap (auto-generated):
- Redwood deliverables: pricing scenarios, SOC2/DPA pack, pilot SOW, KMS matrix, benchmark readout.
- Arcadia deliverables: approver list, regulated datasets, security requirements, budget sign target (Dec 12).
- Schedule: technical ridealong to be scheduled next week for benchmarking and deeper infra Q&A.

References/links mentioned: pricing spreadsheet (will be shared), SOC2 summary (will be attached), pilot SOW template (will be attached).

Notes on transcription quality: medium — a few product nouns transcribed imprecisely (e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache), occasional timestamps approximate.
